audits.title: Survey and audit of the standard of care of diabetic patients in the community of East Dorset
audits.standard: Process and outcome criteria for diabetes care within the last 13 months
audits.setting: 51 general practices in East Dorset (37 visited)

cycle1.result: 44% full eye examination, 25% serum cholesterol, 50% smoking status, 57% foot inspection; over 75% had glycaemic control and blood pressure measured; average HbA1c 8.07%

audits.other_findings: Structure questionnaire showed deficiencies in audit facilities, diabetic register completeness and use of optometrists and chiropodists. Diabetes prevalence 1.61%.
audits.citation: Dunn NR. Survey and audit of the standard of care of diabetic patients in the community of East Dorset. . 1998.

audits.title: Quality of care of patients with diabetes: collation of data from multi-practice audits of diabetes in primary care.
audits.standard: Annual key process measures for diabetes care
audits.setting: Multi-practice audits by 17 medical audit advisory groups (495 practices)

cycle1.result: Annual mean compliance: HbA1c or fructosamine 72.5%, fundi 67.5%, urine 65.8%, blood pressure 87.6%, smoking 71.4%, feet 67.7%, BMI 52.5%, with wide ranges between groups.

audits.other_findings: Diabetes prevalence 1.46%; 50.7% managed by general practice only, 19.1% hospital only, 30.2% shared care.
audits.citation: Khunti K, Baker R, Rumsey M, Lakhani M. Quality of care of patients with diabetes: collation of data from multi-practice audits of diabetes in primary care. Fam Pract. 1999;16(1):54-59. doi:10.1093/fampra/16.1.54. PMID: 10321397.

audits.title: Diabetes management quality improvement in a family practice residency program.
audits.standard: Accepted diabetes care indicators, compared with other Iowa practices
audits.setting: Northeast Iowa Family Practice Clinic, residency training site, Waterloo

cycle1.result: Diabetes care indicator rates measured from Medicare claims and chart abstraction; 1996 figures not given.

audits.intervention: Chart audits, HbA1c reminder cards, educational symposia, endocrinology outreach clinic, resident rotations, diabetes flow sheets, pharmacist interface and nursing foot-examination preparation.

cycle2.result: HbA1c measured in 84% (1997) and 88% (1998) vs 49% and 41% at other Iowa practices.

audits.other_findings: not reported
audits.citation: Sutherland JE, Hoehns JD, O'Donnell B, Wiblin RT. Diabetes management quality improvement in a family practice residency program. J Am Board Fam Pract. 2001;14(4):243-251. PMID: 11458966.

audits.title: Audit of a shared-care program for persons with diabetes: baseline and 3 annual follow-ups.
audits.standard: Programme performance indicators
audits.setting: Shared-care programme with 257 GPs, AUSL Modena

cycle1.result: Glycaemic control indicators 66%-75%; vascular indicators 59%-65%; mean HbA1c 7.6%.

audits.intervention: Shared-care programme between GPs and diabetes services.

cycle2.result: Glycaemic control indicators 83%-90%; vascular indicators 75%-81%; mean HbA1c 7.3%.

audits.other_findings: Similar improvement in disabled and non-disabled patients.

audits.title: Audit of diabetes mellitus in general practice.
audits.standard: Eleven diabetes process and outcome criteria
audits.setting: Seven general practice clinics in Perak

cycle1.result: Inadequacies in nine of eleven criteria; diabetic register in 28.6% of clinics; reminder mechanism in 0%; blood sugar control 21.8%.

audits.intervention: Remedial measures implemented, including diabetic registers and reminder mechanisms.

cycle2.result: Improvements in all criteria; all clinics had a diabetic register; 57.1% had a reminder mechanism; blood sugar control 31.3%.

audits.other_findings: Recording of weight, height, blood pressure, foot examination, fundoscopy, glucose monitoring and urine albumin improved.
audits.citation: Lee TW, Chan SC, Chua WT, Harbinder K, Khoo YL, Ow Yeang YL, et al.. Audit of diabetes mellitus in general practice. Med J Malaysia. 2004;59(3):317-322. PMID: 15727376.

audits.title: Failure of Internet-based audit and feedback to improve quality of care delivered by primary care residents.
audits.standard: National guidelines: HbA1c testing in previous 6 months for diabetes; beta-blocker or diuretic for hypertension
audits.setting: Harvard Vanguard Medical Associates, 14-site multispecialty group, Boston

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention cohort: 76 diabetes and 329 hypertension patients (adherence figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Internet-based audit and feedback: residents given access to their practice profiles on a secure website.

cycle2.result: No discernible effect on adherence to diabetes or hypertension guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Only four of 12 residents accessed their website over a year.
audits.citation: Simon SR, Soumerai SB. Failure of Internet-based audit and feedback to improve quality of care delivered by primary care residents. Int J Qual Health Care. 2005;17(5):427-431. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzi044. PMID: 15831542.

audits.title: The effect of a primary care intervention on management of patients with diabetes and hypertension: a pre-post intervention chart audit.
audits.standard: Process-of-care and outcome targets for diabetes and hypertension
audits.setting: Four Strengthening Primary Care Initiative sites, Nova Scotia

cycle1.result: Diabetes BP target 20.4%, retinopathy screening 33.8%; hypertension systolic target 40.6%.

audits.intervention: Collaborative practice teams with nurse practitioner, alternative physician funding and an information system.

cycle2.result: Diabetes BP target 28.5%, retinopathy screening 41.9%, nephropathy 71.3%; hypertension systolic target 55.3%, diastolic 85.3%.

audits.other_findings: BP checked twice yearly fell from 89.1% to 85.0%; fasting glucose recording rose from 37.7% to 67.1%.
audits.citation: Graham L, Sketris I, Burge F, Edwards L. The effect of a primary care intervention on management of patients with diabetes and hypertension: a pre-post intervention chart audit. Healthc Q. 2006;9(2):62-71. doi:10.12927/hcq..18105. PMID: 16640135.

audits.title: Survey and audit of diabetes care in general practice in south London.
audits.standard: Level of supervision of diabetic patients (standard not stated)
audits.setting: 388 general practices in six family practitioner committee areas, south London

cycle1.result: Survey of 388 practices (69% response): 14% offered mini-clinics, one quarter kept a diabetes register, fewer had a recall system. Audit of 378 patients by 77 doctors showed better supervision of non-insulin dependent diabetics where registers were kept and special arrangements were made.

audits.other_findings: Clinic time set aside was not demonstrably better; barriers were lack of time, no recall system and lack of clinical skills.
audits.citation: Chesover D, Tudor-Miles P, Hilton S. Survey and audit of diabetes care in general practice in south London. Br J Gen Pract. 1991;41(348):282-285. PMID: 1747266.

audits.title: Quality improvement programme for diabetes care in family practice settings in Dubai.
audits.standard: Key clinical indicators for diabetes care (HbA1c <7%, LDL <100 mg/dL, blood pressure)
audits.setting: 16 government primary health care centres, Dubai

cycle1.result: HbA1c <7% in 20.6%; LDL cholesterol <100 mg/dL in 20.8%; mean systolic BP 135.3 mmHg.

audits.intervention: Quality improvement teams, clinical guidelines, information systems, diabetes nurse practitioners and a team approach

cycle2.result: HbA1c <7% in 31.7%; LDL cholesterol <100 mg/dL in 33.6%; mean systolic BP 133.2 mmHg.

audits.other_findings: Recording rates of key clinical indicators also improved significantly.

audits.title: A tale of two audits: statistical process control for improving diabetes care in primary care settings.
audits.standard: Appropriateness of diabetes management against locally agreed guideline criteria
audits.setting: Chronic disease mini-clinics, King Saud City Family and Community Medicine Centre, Riyadh

cycle1.result: Random samples of 30 files every two weeks plotted on p charts; mean non-conformities 5.0 at the start.

audits.intervention: Periodic process audits with statistical process control charts displayed for all staff (feedback).

cycle2.result: Process-measure series: mean non-conformities fell from 5.0 to 1.4; proportion non-conforming fell by 10% within 3 months.

audits.other_findings: Audit series with mixed outcome and process measures detected no change over a year.
audits.citation: Al-Hussein FA. A tale of two audits: statistical process control for improving diabetes care in primary care settings. Qual Prim Care. 2008;16(1):53-60. PMID: 18700079.

audits.setting: Family practice clinics, tertiary care private teaching hospital (Aga Khan University), Karachi

cycle1.result: Only one quarter qualified as excellent or good care; body weight monitored at every visit in 100%; blood glucose advice 79.5%; physical activity advice 27.3%; blood sugar control in 23.9%.

audits.title: Audit of diabetes in general practice.
audits.standard: Practice-agreed standards, e.g. fructosamine <3.5 mmol/l in 90% and <2.8 mmol/l in 70% of under-70s; blood glucose targets in 90%; 100% of new diabetics referred to dietitian and given education
audits.setting: Group general practice, Horfield Health Centre, Bristol (about 13,200 patients)

cycle1.result: Fructosamine <3.5 mmol/l 62% v 90% and <2.8 mmol/l 35% v 70% (n = 149); blood glucose <10 mmol/l in 23% of insulin dependent (n = 48) and <8 mmol/l in 17% of non-insulin dependent (n = 101) v 90%; new patients (n = 32) 59% referred to dietitians and 28% given education v 100%.

audits.other_findings: First audit cycle; authors propose a simple method using disease and attendance registers plus fructosamine for continuing the cycle.
audits.citation: Kemple TJ, Hayter SR. Audit of diabetes in general practice. BMJ. 1991;302(6774):451-453. doi:10.1136/bmj.302.6774.451. PMID: 2004174.

audits.title: Improving management of type 2 diabetes - findings of the Type2Care clinical audit.
audits.standard: Annual cycle of care and diabetes targets (e.g. microalbumin)
audits.setting: Australian general practices (Type2Care audit)

cycle1.result: Mean HbA1c 6.9%.

audits.intervention: Feedback to GPs and a decision support tool.

cycle2.result: Use of annual cycle of care plans increased by 12%; performance improved on all measures; mean HbA1c 6.9%.

audits.other_findings: Greatest gains were in care plan use and microalbumin measurement and targets.

audits.title: Applying Quality Improvement into Systems-based Learning to Improve Diabetes Outcomes in Primary Care.
audits.standard: National patient-centred diabetes quality measures (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Shared Savings Program)
audits.setting: 30 primary care physicians in three accountable care organisations

cycle1.result: Baseline chart audit of documented counselling, side-effect assessment, adherence, A1C and BMI (baseline figures not given).

audits.intervention: Accredited CME: private performance improvement internet course, small-group internet courses and enduring materials.

cycle2.result: Documented side-effect assessment +11%, counselling on risks/benefits +28%, medication adherence +13%, lifestyle modification +8%; documented adherence +24%; A1C -0.16%, BMI -2.1.

audits.other_findings: Enduring materials were also offered to clinicians nationwide who did not take part.
